academic.passage: Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections. This phenomenon is crucial for learning and memory, allowing individuals to acquire new skills and adapt to changes in their environment. Studies indicate that both mental and physical activities can stimulate neuroplastic changes, enhancing cognitive functions. Furthermore, neuroplasticity is not confined to the early stages of life; it continues to occur throughout adulthood, providing lifelong opportunities for personal growth and rehabilitation.
